title: Dataflow-Guided Retrieval Augmentation for Repository-Level Code Completion
budget_tradeoff_detail: Half of total input length is pre-allocated to background knowledge and half to unfinished code by design; DraCo is ~100x faster at prompt construction than RepoCoder while also improving accuracy, but context sizes/snippet counts are not equalized across baselines (Table 5).
confound_note: DraCo vs RepoCoder varies both representation/mechanism (dataflow-graph-guided entity retrieval vs sliding-window similarity retrieval) and the effective context budget (different snippet-count limits per method: unrestricted graph-derived entities vs RepoCoder's fixed K), so budget is not held constant in the central comparison.

title: GraphCoder: Enhancing Repository-Level Code Completion via Code Context Graph-based Retrieval and Language Model

key_numbers.metric: Code EM gain vs RepoCoder (API-level, avg)

budget_tradeoff_detail: Context window split evenly between retrieved snippets and completion context (max 10 snippets); GraphCoder needs one retrieval pass vs RepoCoder's 3 iterations, using fewer total tokens for comparable/better EM (Table 5).
confound_note: Both representation (CCG control/data-dependence graph vs RepoCoder's iterative regeneration-retrieval) and mechanism vary simultaneously; token counts differ between methods rather than being held constant.

title: Enhancing Code Translation in Language Models with Few-Shot Learning via Retrieval-Augmented Generation

key_numbers.metric: CodeBLEU, Granite-34B zero-shot vs one-shot (HPC dataset)

budget_tradeoff_detail: Zero-shot to one-shot retrieval substantially raises CodeBLEU (e.g., Granite-34B 0.237→0.600 on HPC dataset), but no explicit token-budget/cost figures are reported for the added few-shot context.
confound_note: Retrieval mechanism (cosine similarity vs Euclidean distance), embedding model (Nomic-Embed/Starencoder/CodeBERT), and number of shots (0-3) all vary across reported comparisons; shot count changes effective context length without being held fixed as a budget.

title: RepoScope: Leveraging Call Chain-Aware Multi-View Context for Repository-Level Code Generation

key_numbers.metric: Pass@1 on DevEval with Claude-3.5-Haiku (RepoScope vs best baseline)
Pass@1 on CoderEval with DeepSeek-V3 (RepoScope vs DRACO)

budget_tradeoff_detail: Max prompt length capped at 4096 tokens via two-stage per-context-type token allocation; baseline prompt token lengths were tuned to be only approximately comparable (~3679 tokens avg for RepoScope), except RepoCoder/CodeAgent which exceed this due to multi-turn interaction (Evaluation Setup section).
confound_note: Headline comparison (Table 2, RepoScope vs. SimpleRAG/RepoCoder/DRACO/CodeAgent/RLCoder) varies both the context representation/retrieval mechanism and, only approximately, the token budget — not strictly held constant; the internal ablation (Table 3) removing one of the four context views at a time is closer to a budget-matched comparison since it holds the max prompt length (4096) and retrieval pipeline fixed.

title: The Complexity Trap: Simple Observation Masking Is as Efficient as LLM Summarization for Agent Context Management

key_numbers.value: masking 54.8% solve / -52.7% cost vs LLM-summary 53.8% solve / -50.4% cost
7-11% additional cost reduction vs masking/summary alone, +2.6pp solve rate (SWE-bench Verified-50, Qwen3-Coder 480B)

budget_tradeoff_detail: Masking cuts cost ~50-56% relative to the raw (uncompressed) agent while matching or slightly exceeding LLM-summarization's solve rate across five model configurations on SWE-bench Verified (Sec. 4).
confound_note: Central comparison varies the context-management mechanism (fixed-window observation masking vs LLM-generated running summary) at run time; token budget/cost is the measured outcome rather than a held-constant control variable across arms.

title: SWE-Pruner: Self-Adaptive Context Pruning for Coding Agents

key_numbers.metric: SWE-Bench Verified token reduction & resolve rate, Claude Sonnet 4.5
Long Code QA compression vs. accuracy

budget_tradeoff_detail: At matched 4x/8x compression ratios, SWE-Pruner preserves or slightly improves task success (e.g., +1.4pp resolve rate on SWE-Bench Verified with Claude Sonnet 4.5) while cutting tokens 23-54% depending on model/benchmark (Table 1, Sec. 4.2).
confound_note: Table 1 compares pruning methods at fixed compression-ratio targets (4x/8x) — the pruning method is the sole varied factor at matched output budget across compared baselines and SWE-Pruner.

title: ReCUBE: Evaluating Repository-Level Context Utilization in Code Generation
budget_tradeoff_detail: CCE yields +5.79pp external SPR / +8.24pp internal APR / up to +7.56pp overall improvement at roughly comparable or lower per-instance cost than plain agentic exploration ($0.1241 vs $0.1226 on ReCUBE; $0.1166 vs $0.1410 on ReCUBE-large, Table 7), while full-context baselines consume 71K-146K tokens on average
confound_note: central comparison (full-context vs. agent vs. agent+CCE) varies representation, retrieval mechanism, and effective context length/cost together — not a fixed-budget ablation; caller-graph availability, agent tool access, and token consumption all differ simultaneously across arms

title: RepoMirage: Probing Repository Context Reasoning in Code Agents with Perturbations
budget_tradeoff_detail: no token-budget-vs-quality tradeoff reported; only a fixed max-step budget of 250 actions is held constant across conditions (Sec A.2), and perturbations increase file-access ratio 2.49x-5.77x without a corresponding token accounting
confound_note: RepoMirage-Perturb/Extend vary how repository structure is exposed (import indirection, file renaming/relocation, constant externalization) while holding the underlying task fixed; the RepoAnchor comparison then adds an explicit structure-exploration stage, changing both mechanism and effective context organization at once

title: Antaeus: Hunting Repository-Level Logic Vulnerabilities via Context-Grounded LLM Reasoning

key_numbers.metric: True positives detected, AntaeusO4.7 vs. best baselines
Cost per confirmed vulnerability, Antaeus vs. agentic baseline

budget_tradeoff_detail: Antaeus operates in the same cost regime as the agentic baseline (a few hundred dollars total) while detecting 3-5x more true positives (15/28 vs. 3-5/28) at roughly $30 vs. $77 per detected vulnerability (Tables VI/VIII).
confound_note: Table III's central comparison (Antaeus vs. function-level-only and agentic baselines) varies representation (repo-grounded local+global context vs. isolated function or free agentic exploration) and adds a structured reasoning+validation mechanism simultaneously, at roughly comparable but not strictly matched token/cost budgets.

title: Know Before Fix: QA-Driven Repository Knowledge Acquisition for Software Issue Resolution

key_numbers.metric: Average cost per instance, ACQUIRE vs baseline (DeepSeek-V3.2)

budget_tradeoff_detail: ACQUIRE raises average per-instance cost only modestly ($0.073 vs $0.055 baseline on DeepSeek-V3.2) while improving SWE-bench Verified Pass@1 by +4.4pp; cost rises with more QA pairs while performance peaks at N=2 (Fig. 3), and baselines are not cost-matched (e.g. SWE-Debate costs $0.382-$0.738 vs ACQUIRE $0.054-$0.073).
confound_note: The central comparison (ACQUIRE vs. Mini-SWE-Agent and other baselines, Table I) varies both the knowledge-acquisition mechanism and resulting context content/cost simultaneously, not a budget-matched ablation; only the internal ACQUIRE-Proposal/ACQUIRE-FreeQ ablations (Table II) hold the framework fixed while varying the acquisition strategy.

title: CodeNib: A Multi-View Data System for Serving Repository Context to Coding Agents
benchmarks: CodeNib Base (derived from SWE-bench Verified and SWE-bench Multilingual, 100 snapshots)

key_numbers.value: graph updates 8.7x faster, vector updates 25.4x faster than rebuild at median
4.7x median per-request latency ratio on 63% of 1,000 matched requests
50-87% fewer tokens than grep/read baseline within a 5% localization-quality margin (AnswerRecall@5), across 5 agent models

budget_tradeoff_detail: Eager/Compact context policies (frozen top-10 dense-retrieved code blocks) cut trajectory tokens 50-87% versus a grep/read baseline while staying within a 5% localization-quality margin (AnswerRecall@5), across five agent models (Sec. 7.4).
confound_note: Eager vs Compact holds retrieved candidates identical (same top-10 dense ranking) and isolates the context-retention/delivery policy (frozen injection vs one-time deterministic history rewrite) as a true budget-matched ablation; the further comparison against grep/read varies both retrieval mechanism and token budget together, conflating retrieval quality with delivery policy.
